title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-scratchpad-megan-ortiz
content:
Incident summary:
- Date/time observed: 2025-02-14 22:03 UTC (first alert)
- Impact: ~8% increased 5xx rate for hosted-api in eu-west-1; automated smart-routing fallback engaged and routed ~12% of requests to us-east-1 variant for a brief window.
- User-visible effect: elevated latency for some requests (~600-900ms vs baseline 120-250ms) and a handful of 502/503 spikes.
- Current status: mitigation applied (revert routing policy -> regional strict), monitoring in steady state but want root cause + hard fixes.

Notes / timeline (working):
- 22:03 UTC: PagerDuty alert (eu-west-1 endpoint 5xx spike). Initial triage by on-call SRE (Liam). Router reports high error ratio for model redwood-open-3b-quant.
- 22:06 UTC: Smart-routing policy triggered fallback to compatible variant redwood-open-3b (non-quant) in us-east-1 due to a sudden drop in available pods (OOMs reported on dedicated pool).
- 22:08-22:20 UTC: Canary and retries increased; downstream services logged intermittent: "kv-cache-miss -> cold-start" and "rpc: connection reset by peer" for several routing hops.
- 22:30 UTC: Reverted to regional-strict routing to stop cross-region failovers. Error rate returned to baseline by 22:35.

Commands and queries I ran (most useful outputs below):
- Check router health & policy state:
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" "https://admin.internal/routers/eu-west-1/state" | jq '.'
  -> showed policy: smart-routing: enabled, fallback_policy: regional-fallback, last_changed: "2025-02-14T22:05:12Z"

- Inspecting pod OOM events (k8s):
  kubectl -n serving-prod get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Pod -o wide | grep redwood-open-3b-quant
  kubectl -n serving-prod logs redwood-open-3b-quant-pod-7f8c --since=1h | egrep "OOMKilled|out of memory|Killed process"
  -> several OOMKilled entries on node gcu-45, approx 22:02-22:04

- Router trace for a sample failing request (request id: req-20250214-22-04-211):
  - router: eu-west-1/route-137 -> chosen pool: quant-pool-2 (pod unhealthy) -> fallback to us-east-1/variant-nonquant
  - logs: "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer"
  - client saw status 503 after 3 retries

- KV cache inspection (redis):
  redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 INFO | egrep "used_memory_human|connected_clients"
  redis-cli -h redis-eu-01 GET "kv:prefix:session:abc123"
  -> small number of cache misses but not huge; cache pressure ok.

- Check autoscaler decisions:
  SELECT timestamp, target_replicas, actual_replicas FROM autoscaler_audit WHERE region='eu-west-1' AND service='quant-pool' AND timestamp > '2025-02-14 21:50'
  -> observed scale-down event at 21:59 to 3 replicas from 6, then failed scale-up to 6 (insufficient nodes) at 22:01.

Error snippets collected:
- "OOMKilled: Process killed due to memory" (node gcu-45)
- "rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection reset by peer"
- "router: chosen backend returned 5xx: upstream read timeout"
- Client error: "502 Bad Gateway"
- Admin UI log: "policy-evaluator: fallback triggered: capacity_insufficient (cpu/mem)"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Under-provisioning + aggressive scale-down: a scale-down event shortly before the traffic spike removed quant pods and cluster autoscaler couldn't reclaim nodes fast enough -> router saw many backends unhealthy and triggered cross-region fallback. (High confidence)
2) A regression in the quant runtime caused OOMs on a subset of models when encountering longer sequences, leading to cascade of pod restarts. (Medium confidence)
3) Redis/kv cache transient spike created many cold KVs increasing memory and pushing pods over OOM threshold (low-to-medium confidence).
4) Network flakiness between eu-west-1 and internal control-plane (unlikely: control-plane logs are clean but need deeper packet captures) (low confidence)

Immediate follow-ups done:
- Reverted routing policy to regional-strict at 22:30 to avoid cross-region tail latency and egress costs.
- Opened a k8s investigation ticket: K8S-5432 (assigned to infra oncall).
- Increased desired capacity for quant-pool in eu-west-1 (manual override) from 3->6 and warned autoscaler team.
- Kept an eye on OOM nodes (migrated a few pods off gcu-45).

Potential fixes / next steps:
- Short-term (days):
  - Add a safety buffer to autoscaler for quant pools during peak windows (increase min_replicas to avoid scale-down race). Owner: infra.
  - Add a health-check cooldown in router: avoid triggering cross-region fallback unless contiguous failures > N (increase threshold). Owner: serving-runtime.
  - Add a more explicit OOM metric alert (OOMs per node > 1/min) to catch before routing fallback. Owner: observability.

- Medium-term (weeks):
  - Run a quant-runtime stress test with long-sequence synthetic inputs to reproduce and fix potential regression. Owner: serving-runtime/applied-ml.
  - Investigate memory accounting in the quant allocator (possible leak/regression after recent kernel changes). Owner: serving-runtime.
  - Improve autoscaler cluster holo-check: ensure scale-up path uses spillover zones/nodes instead of completing scale-downs during transient load. Owner: platform-engineering.

Observations & gotchas:
- The router's fallback policy is currently sensitive to short windows of increased 5xx; we should tune cooldown windows to prevent cross-region churn (cost + latency).
- Cross-region fallbacks increase tail latencies quickly (network + cold caches) - we saw ~2x latency on routed requests.
- Admin UI shows a helpful breadcrumb: "fallback triggered due to capacity_insufficient (eu-west-1 quant-pool)" which matches autoscaler logs.

Open questions / things to verify:
- Were there any recent config changes to the quant runtime/container image deployed to eu-west-1 around 2025-02-14 20:00-21:30? (check CI/CD deploy history)
- Any scheduled maintenance on nodes in eu-west-1 that might have caused simultaneous node drains? (check infra calendar + GCP events)
- Was there a traffic pattern change (longer prompts, more embeddings) that increased memory per-request? (query request histogram)
- Do we need to change fallback policy to prefer regional cold spin-up instead of cross-region failover? Might be better for consistency.

Notes for postmortem:
- Incident start: 2025-02-14 22:03 UTC. Mitigation (routing revert + capacity bump) by 22:30. Resolved ~22:35.
- Primary contributors: infra-autoscaler decision + OOMs on quant-pool.
- Action items: autoscaler min buffer, router cooldown tuning, stress tests for quant runtime.

Quick links (internal):
- k8s events dump (gcs): gs://redwood-ops/incidents/2025-02-14/eu-west-1-k8s-events.txt
- Router traces: https://tracing.internal/r/req-20250214-22-04-211
- Autoscaler audit: https://sql.internal/queries/auto-audit?job=K8S-5432
- CI deploy history: https://ci.internal/pipelines/redwood-open-3b

Todo (me / followups):
- [ ] Pull node-level dmesg for gcu-45 and adjacent nodes and attach to K8S-5432 (due 2025-02-16)
- [ ] Run long-sequence GC/stress test against quant image pinned to sha: sha256:ab12... (due 2025-02-18)
- [ ] Propose router cooldown change (PR draft) and run canary (due 2025-02-20)

Scratchpad/hypothesis experiments I want to run:
- Reproduce OOM locally with container profile using 4x longer prompt sequences (tool: local-infer-runner). Script:
  ./local-infer-runner --model redwood-open-3b-quant --sequence-length 16384 --batch-size 1 --duration 10m

- Simulated autoscaler churn:
  ./simulate-traffic --rps 1200 --p95-len 2k --zone eu-west-1 --duration 15m
  then observe scale decisions in autoscaler-audit table.

If anyone else sees additional logs or has context (deploys, maintenance, known kv spikes), please drop them here.

-- Megan Ortiz
